notable_absence.finding: GROUP BY, like the other SELECT sub-clauses in this batch (HAVING, LETTING, GROUP AS), carries no Prerequisites/privilege table of its own - access control is asserted once at the FROM/keyspace level (see from.json), not re-stated per downstream clause. This is a structural, not anomalous, absence: it confirms the credential-type model gates keyspace access, not individual query-clause usage.

cross_component_finding: The Limitations section ties GROUP BY directly to index selection behavior: 'A query needs a predicate on a leading index key to ensure that the optimizer can select a secondary index for the query... This is usually only necessary in queries which do not otherwise have a WHERE clause; for example, some GROUP BY and aggregate queries.' This is a genuine Query-engine <-> Index-service interaction, but it describes optimizer behavior rather than an access-control or product-boundary relation, so it is noted here rather than forced into a relation.
